$comment: federation-contract policy — the ramp + ratchet for scripts/gate_federation_contract.py
(gate-federation-contract). governance/naming-and-addressing.md, 'What must actually
agree': registration/manifest.json integration.remoteEntry, the bundler `base`, the
chart's Ingress `path`, and the web server's location/alias PLUS where the Dockerfile
puts the build are ONE contract.
WHY A RATCHET AND NOT A FLAT `|| true`.
naming-and-addressing.md is right that 'a warning tier is a `|| true` spelled politely'
— gate-authz's trailing `|| true` and gate-identifier's never-set opt-in flag both
produced a check that could not fail. This file is deliberately NOT that shape:
* A repo NOT listed under ratchet.knownFailing is ENFORCED AT FULL STRENGTH from day
one. There is no state in which a new remote lands with a broken serve contract and
the gate stays quiet.
* A listed repo is held ONLY for the exact layers named in its entry. A finding in any
OTHER layer of a listed repo still FAILS. Fixing one layer and breaking a different
one is caught.
* The list is a worklist with a named owner and a flip condition, not an exemption.
Each entry says what is wrong and what fixes it.
WHY IT SHIPPED RAMPED AT ALL. Measured against every repo's LIVE DEFAULT BRANCH on
2026-08-23, at full strength: 15 repos CHECKED, 14 FAIL, 1 clean (fuzeservice); 3
SKIPPED. A gate that reds 14 of 15 repos the day it lands gets disabled within the
fortnight and is then worth nothing — the same disease naming-and-addressing.md
diagnoses, arriving by the other road. The ratchet keeps the gate live and enforcing on
everything new while the named backlog is burned down.
TEACHING THE GATE A NEW DIALECT IS ALSO A WIDENING FIX.
The Node/Express reader made three carved-out repos checkable at once, and the count
moved in BOTH directions: fuzex left the worklist entirely (it was correct all along —
a literal mount prefix, a root from a Dockerfile ENV, and the build copied exactly
there), while fuzemarket's vague 'no web-server config' became a precise, actionable
L4a. Never assume repos sharing an architecture share a verdict; each was read.
RESURVEY AFTER EVERY CHECK THAT WIDENS WHAT THE GATE CAN SEE.
Making vendored-copy ownership POSITIONAL rather than slug-scoped made a whole class of
L1 defect visible for the first time — a copy whose SLUG had drifted used to read as
'a different product' and be skipped, so the check turned itself off exactly when it had
something to say. fuzeagent gained an L1 finding the moment that landed, and because its
entry listed only L2 the ratchet correctly FAILED it on the newly-visible layer. That is
the ratchet working, not a bug — but it means a ramp built before a widening fix is stale
by construction. Re-measure; never carry a count across a change to the gate's reach.
THIS LIST IS BUILT FROM LIVE DEFAULT BRANCHES, AND THAT CORRECTION MATTERS.
The first version was built from local clones, and ALL EIGHTEEN were stale — several by
days, several checked out on feature branches. Two entries were wrong in opposite and
equally damaging directions: fuzeservice was listed as failing when it had already been
fixed (a free pass on a layer it no longer violates, and the ratchet's stale-entry notice
is the only thing that would ever have said so), and fuzepicker was recorded CLEAN while
live master carried a wrong-prefix mount (a repo wrongly marked clean is enforced at full
strength and reds unexpectedly). Rebuild this list from fresh clones of each repo's live
default branch — never from whatever is on disk.
TO FLIP: set mode to "fail". Do it when ratchet.knownFailing is empty, or empty enough
that the remainder is a deliberate, written-down decision. Removing a repo's entry is
how a fix is banked — the gate prints a notice when an entry no longer matches any
finding, so a stale entry cannot quietly re-open the ramp.
modes:  "ratchet" — shipped default, described above
"fail"    — the ratchet is ignored entirely; every finding fails
"warn"    — everything warns. An escape hatch for a bisect, NOT a rollout mode.
A repo with NO policy file gets mode "fail": deleting this file must not be a way to
silence the gate.
flipCondition: ratchet.knownFailing is empty (or its remainder is a written decision), then set mode to "fail".

ratchet.surveyedAgainst: each repo's LIVE default branch, freshly cloned — not local checkouts
ratchet.surveyResult: 15 CHECKED / 13 FAIL / 2 clean (fuzeservice, fuzex); 3 SKIPPED (fuzefront — no registration/manifest.json at the repo root, it is the host; fuzehub and fuzeplan — integration.type: iframe). Re-measured after the Node/Express dialect landed, not carried over: fuzex proved CORRECT once readable and left the worklist; fuzemarket's L4a became a precise finding instead of 'no web-server config'; fuzemerchandize's L4a became UNREADABLE (a dynamic root); fuzebi and fuzeexecutive kept L4b but for the truthful reason once the serving image and its final stage were scoped correctly.

fuzepicker.note: WRONG-PREFIX MOUNT, and the fifth instance of one root error. #88 (merged 06:41:38Z) set picker-app/nginx.conf to `location ^~ /apps/fuzepicker/ { alias /usr/share/nginx/html/; }` while the manifest, vite `base` and the Ingress all serve /apps/picker/ — so the block never matches and remoteEntry.js falls through to the SPA catch-all. The alias and the flat COPY are CORRECT for the design chosen; only the prefix is wrong. #89 fixes it with a one-word diff. Do NOT change the Dockerfile and do NOT touch the slug: #88 reasoned from backend/src/routes/appRegistry.ts, the CI/local-only fallback gated on APP_REGISTRY_LOCAL_ADAPTER=1 (default off); production is backend/applications/src/app-registry/service.ts, which stores `slug: row.slug` verbatim.

fuzesocial.note: packages/fuzesocial-ui/Dockerfile copies dist flat to /usr/share/nginx/html while base is /apps/fuzesocial/, and its `location = /remoteEntry.js` matches the bare path, not the based one. Fix either by copying the build to /usr/share/nginx/html/apps/fuzesocial, or by adding an alias mount the way fuzeservice now does.

fuzeagent.note: L1: deploy/helm/fuzeagent/files/registration/manifest.json declares slug "agent" while the root declares "fuzeagent", AND still carries the old cross-origin https://fuzeagent.prod.fuzefront.com/remoteEntry.js. The init container POSTs the VENDORED copy, so this registers a SECOND, WRONG app rather than serving a broken one. Fix the vendored copy, never the root — the slug is immutable. FuzeAgent#177 is in flight for exactly this; remove L1 from this entry when it merges (the gate prints a stale-entry notice once it no longer fires). This finding was INVISIBLE until the ownership rule became positional: the stale slug made the copy read as a different product. L2: services/ui-react/vite.config.ts has base '/' with the default assetsDir, so the entry builds at /assets/remoteEntry.js while the manifest advertises /apps/fuzeagent/remoteEntry.js.

fuzedeploy.note: frontend/Dockerfile copies /app/build flat to /usr/share/nginx/html; base is /apps/deploy/.

fuzebi.note: frontend/Dockerfile is a static landing page with no build stage at all (its own header says so), so nothing places the frontend-mfe bundle in the image. Registration is disabled in prod for the same reason.

fuzecall.note: No Dockerfile COPYs frontend/'s build output into a served image.

fuzeexecutive.note: No Dockerfile COPYs frontend-mfe's build output into a served image.

fuzefinance.note: Only backend/ and landing/ Dockerfiles exist; frontend-mfe has no image.

fuzekeys.note: LAYER-4 POSITIVE CONTROL, layer-2 defect. Its `location ^~ /apps/fuzekeys/ { alias ...; }` and its `COPY --from=build-mfe /app/dist-mfe /usr/share/nginx/html/apps/fuzekeys` are exactly right. But frontend/vite.config.ts sets no `assetsDir`, so Vite's default `assets` applies and @originjs/vite-plugin-federation emits the entry at ${assetsDir}/${filename} (dist/index.js:1231, default at :1777) — i.e. /apps/fuzekeys/assets/remoteEntry.js, while the manifest advertises /apps/fuzekeys/remoteEntry.js. Fix: add `assetsDir: ''` to build, per community-templates/mfe-starter/vite.config.ts note 4. Do NOT touch the slug.

fuzemarket.note: L1 is the serious one and is exactly what the vendored-copy check exists for: registration/manifest.json was corrected to /apps/market/remoteEntry.js, but deploy/helm/fuzemarket/files/registration/manifest.json — THE COPY THE CLUSTER ACTUALLY SERVES — still carries https://fuzemarket.fuze.internal/dist/remoteEntry.js, an RFC 6761 special-use name that resolves for nobody. The fix landed in the file people read and not in the file that deploys. Its L1 is being fixed separately in FuzeMarket#84 — drop L1 from this entry when that merges. L4a is REAL AND UNFIXED: server/server.js is a hand-rolled Node server whose serveStatic() joins the request path straight onto ROOT (= /app/site, from the Dockerfile's `ENV STATIC_DIR`), i.e. a mount at `/`, while the Dockerfile copies the MF build to /app/site/dist. So /apps/market/remoteEntry.js resolves to /app/site/apps/market and 404s live. Either mount /apps/market/ onto /app/site/dist or move the build to /app/site/apps/market — both valid, pick deliberately; do not change the Dockerfile by reflex.

fuzemerchandize.note: L4a is UNREADABLE, not absent: server/app.mjs:127 does `app.use(express.static(staticDir, {...}))` where staticDir is threaded in at runtime and no Dockerfile ENV or chart value pins it, so the serve path cannot be verified statically. Make it a literal or set it from a Dockerfile `ENV`. L4b: no final-stage COPY places frontend/'s build into the image at all.

fuzecontact.note: helm/fuzecontact/templates/ingress.yaml uses `{{ .path }}` with no `default "..."`, so the shipped route is not readable from the chart. Fix: give the template a literal default.

fuzesales.note: Same as fuzecontact — a templated ingress path with no literal default.
